related_questions.question: What diseases does Neisseria gonorrhoeae cause?
related_questions.snippet: Untreated N. gonorrhoeae infections can lead to complications and sequelae in women, such as pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), ectopic pregnancy, and infertility. Complications in men are scrotal swelling, urethral stricture and infertility. Neonatal conjunctivitis (eye infection) if untreated may lead to blindness.

text_blocks.snippet: Neisseria gonorrhoeae bacteria causes the sexually transmitted infection known as gonorrhea. This infection can affect various parts of the body, including the genitals, rectum, and throat. While often asymptomatic, especially in women, gonorrhea can lead to serious complications if left untreated.
Here's a more detailed look at the disease and its effects:

list.title: Transmission:
list.snippet: Gonorrhea is spread through sexual contact, including vaginal, anal, and oral sex.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: In men, symptoms may include a painful or burning sensation when urinating, or a white, yellow, or green discharge from the penis. In women, symptoms can be mild or absent, but may include increased vaginal discharge, pain or burning during urination, or bleeding between periods.

list.title: Complications:
list.snippet: If left untreated, gonorrhea can lead to various complications, including:
Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) in women: This can damage the fallopian tubes and uterus, potentially causing infertility or ectopic pregnancy, according to Mayo Clinic.
Epididymitis in men: Inflammation of the epididymis, a coiled tube at the back of the testicle.
Joint infections: Gonorrhea can spread to the joints, causing pain and swelling.
Disseminated gonococcal infection (DGI): A more serious, life-threatening condition where the bacteria spreads through the bloodstream, potentially causing arthritis and other inflammations.
Infection in newborns: Gonorrhea can be passed from mother to child during childbirth, potentially causing eye infections (gonococcal conjunctivitis) or even blindness.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: Gonorrhea is curable with antibiotics. However, it's important to complete the full course of medication as directed, even if symptoms improve.

list.title: Prevention:
list.snippet: Practicing safe sex, including using condoms, is crucial in preventing gonorrhea and other STIs.
